messages.author: Dulal Mondal
messages.body:
Dear Experts,
I have created time series data externally. From them I calculate average
life time using the following command
readdata fortranpath2.dat
runanalysis lifetime out lt2.dat lifetime fortranpath2.dat:2
go
Then I get an average life time of 2.0976 units. (is the unit in ps?). I
got another file as crv.
I uploaded the two files.
>From the crv file it is found that mydata decorellate at 6th frames. I have
200000 frames and a time step between two consecutive frames is 5 ps. How
can I calculate life time?
Another problem is I am trying to calculate time correlation using the
following command
readdatafortranpath2.dat
timecorr vec1 fortranpath2.dat:2 out v1.out order 2
go
But I get the following error message.
INPUT: Reading input from 'timecor.in'
[readdata fortranpath2.dat]
Reading 'fortranpath2.dat' as Standard Data File with name
'fortranpath2.dat'
DataFile fortranpath2.dat has 2 columns, 200000 lines.
Read 2 data sets.
[timecorr fortranpath2.dat:2 out v1.out order 2]
Error: no vec1 given, ignoring command
Error: Could not setup analysis [timecorr]
1 errors encountered reading input.
TIME: Total execution time: 0.0806 seconds.
Error: Error(s) occurred during execution.
Thanking you
~
-- 
*With regards,*
*Dulal Mondal,*

*Department of Chemistry,*
*IIT Kharagpur, Kharagpur 721302.*

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Mar 21, 2023, Dulal Mondal via AMBER wrote:
>
>readdatafortranpath2.dat
> timecorr vec1 fortranpath2.dat:2 out v1.out order 2
As the error message indcates, the "timecorr" action deals with two
*vectors*, looking at angular and distance correlations relevant to NMR, to
fluorescence polarization decay, and other similar situations. It is not
designed to look at scalar data. See the Manual for details.
....dac
